scope: compare two gamestate captures to separate session-varying bytes from stable header bytes

comparison.offset_0_to_9: different between captures (8b89018f018f8b8b8b8b vs b6b43cb23cb2b6b6b6b6) - these bytes vary with the session key, so they are the contaminated prefix

conclusions: the real, session-stable header begins at offset 10 with the byte 0x03
the ten bytes before it are key-shift contamination and must be ignored when reading structure
0x03 followed by four zero bytes is stable across sessions, so it is either a service opcode or a small sequence/type field
0x03 does not match svc_configstring(2) or svc_serverCommand(4) or SV_WIRE_SERVERCOMMAND(1), so the reliable-command decomposition does not apply to these ten bytes either
next: capture a third time and also record client_t.reliableSequence/reliableSent at the same moment so the stable 03 00 00 00 00 can be matched against a candidate field (for example command type 3 + sequence 0)
test whether 0x03 is a message type used by the 1649370 client's netchan wrapper rather than by svc_* (grep the 2697 source for other opcode families)
if 0x03 turns out to be a wrapper type, replay with opcode 3 + zero sequence + the recovered map/configstring body
